data.trust_score_explanation: Reliable newspaper with professional editorial standards, but still requires article-level verification.

Award-winning independent digital publication focused on the international politics of the climate crisis, with named authors and disclosed funding.

Cross-check individual claims against primary sources (IPCC reports, peer-reviewed studies) for high-stakes decisions.
Long-established newspaper with a dedicated editorial code and corrections policy. Opinion content is clearly labelled and separated from news reporting.
Public broadcaster with formal editorial standards, but headline framing and story selection have drawn criticism from multiple sides. Verify emotionally-charged headlines against the full article.
Official communications channel of the United Nations. Useful for institutional positions, but is not an independent news source and rarely covers criticism of the UN itself.
The UN body responsible for assessing climate science. Reports go through an extensive multi-government and scientific review process.
Advocacy-oriented outlet with limited editorial transparency and unclear sourcing on several articles. Treat claims as a starting point, not a citation.
International news agency known for rigorous sourcing and neutral, wire-service style reporting.
Partisan outlet with a documented history of misleading headlines; claims require independent cross-verification.
Satirical publication; content is intentionally fictional and should never be treated as factual reporting.
